description: Phase 5 — Measured token benchmark. A reproducible benchmark/ harness + `npm run benchmark` using the pure-JS gpt-tokenizer, measuring ADX source vs an equivalent React implementation across understand / modify-style / add-prop tasks, writing a results table. Independent of FEAT-003/004 but should measure the shipped fixture; order it after the compiler work so the ADX fixture it measures is final.
steps: Create benchmark/ with: tasks.json (the three tasks and the file sets each measures — understand: ADX manifest.json+structure.adx+behavior.adx.js+style.adx.css vs React UserCard.tsx+UserCard.module.css; modify-style: ADX style.adx.css vs UserCard.module.css; add-prop: ADX manifest.json+structure.adx+behavior.adx.js vs UserCard.tsx[+types.ts]); react/ (a COMMITTED, hand-written React equivalent of fixtures/user-card meeting the equivalence rule: same DOM structure and visible text, same props with same required/optional/defaults, same styling surface/classes); adx/ (copy or symlink of the measured ADX fixture).

Create benchmark/run.ts: factor the tokenizing+aggregation into a pure measure(fileSets): Results function (so it is unit-testable with in-memory strings and a stubbed encoder). run.ts loads tasks.json, reads each file, tokenizes with gpt-tokenizer using the o200k_base encoder (print which encoder was used), sums per task per framework, computes savings = (react - adx) / react, prints a table to stdout and writes benchmark/results.json. A missing fixture or encoder import failure throws a plain Node error (NOT [ADX]).

Add gpt-tokenizer as a devDependency pinned to an exact version (pure JS, MIT). Add package.json script "benchmark": "tsc -p tsconfig.json && node dist/benchmark/run.js". Ensure benchmark/ is NOT added to the package.json files allowlist (dev-only, never published). Add benchmark/README.md documenting how to reproduce and a short 'Equivalence' note recording what parity was checked between the ADX and React fixtures.

Add test/benchmark-measure.test.ts exercising the pure measure() with tiny in-memory strings and a stubbed encoder, asserting the per-task sums and the savings math (independent of real model token counts). Confirm tsconfig includes benchmark/ so `tsc` emits dist/benchmark/run.js (adjust include/exclude as needed without breaking the published dist layout).
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` tsc-clean and `npm test` green including test/benchmark-measure.test.ts and all prior tests.
`npm run benchmark` runs end-to-end, prints a per-task table naming the encoder used, and writes benchmark/results.json with understand/modify-style/add-prop savings numbers.
The React fixture under benchmark/react/ is committed and is a faithful equivalent of the ADX fixture (same DOM/text, props, styling surface), with the equivalence documented in benchmark/README.md.
benchmark/ is absent from the package.json `files` allowlist.
findings:
SHIPPED. Reproducible token benchmark via `npm run benchmark`. `npm run build` tsc-clean; `npm test` green at 170 tests (165 prior + 5 new in test/benchmark-measure.test.ts); `npm run benchmark` runs end-to-end, prints a per-task table naming the encoder, and writes benchmark/results.json.

MEASURED SAVINGS (gpt-tokenizer o200k_base; savings = (react - adx) / react) — FOR FEAT-006 DOCS:
- understand:    ADX 542 vs React 627 tokens => 13.6% saved (0.13556618819776714)
- modify-style:  ADX 254 vs React 293 tokens => 13.3% saved (0.13310580204778158)
- add-prop:      ADX 288 vs React 334 tokens => 13.8% saved (0.1377245508982036)
Per-file (o200k_base): ADX manifest.json=115, structure.adx=83, behavior.adx.js=90, style.adx.css=254 (understand sum 542). React UserCard.tsx=334, UserCard.module.css=293 (understand sum 627).

HONESTY-RULE INPUT FOR FEAT-006: the measured range (~13-14% on the three tasks) is FAR BELOW the hand-estimated headline "Token Efficiency: 65-85% reduction vs. traditional frameworks" (docs/comparison.md Summary; per-task estimates 73%/81%/86%/95%). Per the design's honesty rule, FEAT-006 MUST add a "Measured (M2)" section to docs/comparison.md + docs/token-efficiency.md with this real table, keep the old numbers but mark them "estimated, pre-measurement", and adjust the README/architecture/comparison headline claim to the MEASURED range (~13-14% on the measured single-component tasks) with a pointer to `npm run benchmark`. Rationale the docs should note: the equivalence rule forces a faithful MINIMAL React single-component equivalent (one .tsx + one CSS module), so the gap is modest at single-component scale; the larger estimated gains assume multi-file/multi-component React overhead not captured by this fixture.

IMPLEMENTATION NOTES:
- benchmark/ layout: tasks.json (3 tasks + file sets, declares encoder o200k_base), adx/ (a COPY of fixtures/user-card's four files — re-copy if the fixture changes), react/ (committed hand-written equivalent: UserCard.tsx with inline UserCardProps + UserCard.module.css; no separate types.ts needed), run.ts, README.md (reproduce + Equivalence note), results.json (committed reproducible sample).
- run.ts factors a PURE measure(fileSets, encode, encoderName): Results (plus sumFiles + formatTable). measure takes in-memory file contents + an injected Encoder, so test/benchmark-measure.test.ts exercises it with a word-splitting stub encoder (asserts per-task sums, savings math, empty-react => 0 savings no divide-by-zero, encoder called per file, table names encoder) WITHOUT real token counts. run.ts's main() dynamic-imports gpt-tokenizer/encoding/o200k_base (plain Node error on import failure, NOT [ADX]); the direct-run guard (import.meta.url === process.argv[1]) keeps main() from firing when the test imports the module.
- gpt-tokenizer pinned EXACT at 2.9.0 (pure JS, MIT) as a devDependency. Imported via subpath 'gpt-tokenizer/encoding/o200k_base' (resolves through the package's './*' export wildcard; named export `encode`).
- BUILD/LAYOUT DECISION (deviation from the pinned script string, honoring the HARD 'do not break the published dist layout' constraint): a single `tsc -p tsconfig.json` cannot emit BOTH dist/cli.js (src at dist root, rootDir:src) AND dist/benchmark/run.js — including benchmark/ in the main tsconfig forces tsc's computed rootDir to the project root and relocates everything to dist/src/* (breaks bin dist/cli.js + main dist/index.js). SOLUTION: a separate tsconfig.benchmark.json (rootDir '.', include ['benchmark/**/*.ts'], outDir dist => dist/benchmark/run.js); the `benchmark` script is "tsc -p tsconfig.benchmark.json && node dist/benchmark/run.js". The main tsconfig.json now also excludes 'benchmark'. Net effect matches the acceptance criteria exactly: `npm run build` + published dist layout UNCHANGED (verified: clean `npm run build` emits NO dist/benchmark/, dist/cli.js + dist/index.js intact), and `npm run benchmark` still runs end-to-end.
- files allowlist UNCHANGED (dist, tokens, README.md) — benchmark/ source is NOT in it; dist/ is gitignored so a clean build+publish never ships dist/benchmark/. results.json committed as a reproducible sample; dist/benchmark/ stays gitignored via the existing dist/ rule.
- eslint clean on benchmark/run.ts + test/benchmark-measure.test.ts (full-repo `npm run lint` not run — known prohibitively slow in this worktree, same as prior features). Docs NOT touched (doc-sync is FEAT-006). Committed locally; not pushed.
